summary: PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16 is a careful extraction with a thorough review, and its mathematics stands. I re-read the whole published article (Ann. of Math. 184 (2016), 949–990; the hash matches) against all 188 items. I recomputed the D = 12 and D = 28 cycles, the Hirzebruch–Zagier formula for all p < 600, the four numerical instances of Theorem 4, and the checks behind E3, E4, E5, E24, E26 and part of E28. The 34 recorded mistakes are genuine, and I found no new mistake in the paper. The work breaks in 16 findings: 6 medium and 10 low. Medium: (1) the review rewrote item 141 with a false implication (the product of two positive fundamental discriminants need not be coprime to them or fundamental). (2) The review removed the Rankin–Selberg norm identity that the corrected (6.6), and so Theorem 2, needs; route 5 still promises it to AL.3, but no item carries it. (3) The genus character on binary forms (items 101–102) duplicates Bruinier–Ehlen–Yang 21's GN.2 owner. (4) Route 9 re-plans upstream FuchsianOrbifolds work: area(F) = π/3, the signature of PSL(2,Z), and the cofinite case of (2.8). (5) Bessel functions, the Kloosterman sum and the Laplacian are routed to AS and ES.0, whose texts do not plan them, while QM.2/QM.3 name them and now have nodes for them. (6) The errata file and the extraction reuse ids E5, E6 and E11–E14 for different or conflicting records, so the register has 48 entries for 34 mistakes. Low: sourceVersions missing (the errata file fails check_errata); statuses that should be planned (Duke's theorem at GN.4, E(z,s) at AS.1/AS.2, the Maass functional equation at AL.2); unused library declarations (narrow-class kernel, the unit theorem, stabiliser orders, orbit representatives, Hecke slash sums); item 14's cross-ratio formula claimed as library; no item for the Kronecker character χ_d; dangling references to the 31 removed items; no item for the numerical instances of Theorem 4; inconsistent owners for Siegel's and Burgess's bounds.
checked: Authorship and independence. The review REV-PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16 is by Claude Code cc-2aeb03 (issue #1171, commit 75afde94, 23 September). The errata record research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16.json/.md is by cc-fb70e5 (commit 595309a0), and its review REV-ERRATA-PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16 by codex-7e92bd (commit 91e7e82f). The string cc-f805bf occurs in none of the result, .md, .review.json, the review report, the errata files or the errata review. This session did none of that work.

Disclosure. This session red-teamed PAPER-KHAYUTIN-19 (PR #4789) and wrote FIX-RT-AREA-automorphic-1, which edited AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.1/AS.2/AS.4, AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF and AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL stages and MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.6/MP.7 scope. Findings 5 and 8 cite AS and AL stage texts. They quote those texts at the review's commit 75afde94, which predates that fix, and they ask for no change to this session's files. No finding touches Khayutin 19, which has no item overlapping this paper (checked: its Siegel/Duke-type items are toral-joinings statements).

Every item's statement, locator and status read, with the pre-review text (commit 7d792492) compared for the 29 items whose statement the review changed and the 31 items it removed. Searches of the pinned libraries for items marked missing: hyperbolic Laplacian, Kloosterman sums, Maass forms, non-holomorphic Eisenstein series, binary quadratic forms and reduction, minus continued fractions (Mathlib has only GenContFract), Pell/fundamental units, theta multipliers and half-integral weight, Bessel and Whittaker functions, Siegel's and Burgess's theorems, class-number formulas, limit sets, Nielsen regions and Gauss–Bonnet, Hecke operators, the area of the modular domain, stabiliser orders, orbit representatives and SL(2,Z) generators. None found for the first group; the finds are reported in findings 4 and 9–13.

Stage texts read in full at the review's commit and now: GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2–GN.4; AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0–AS.6; MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.0–MP.8; AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.0–AF.5; AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.0–AL.5; AnalyticNumberTheory AN.0–AN.4; GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.5; ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod ES.0; QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.2–QM.3; ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.1; and the Tau Ceti FuchsianOrbifolds README (Layers 0–6) and Multiquadratic roadmap extract.

Packets read for overlap (all partial, all created after the 23 September acceptance): GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic (GN.3/GN.4 coverage; it does not yet use this paper), AnalyticNumberTheory--AN.0 (AN.2–AN.4 nodes, Siegel/Kedlaya source issue), ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod (no Kloosterman or Burgess node), AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors, MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.0 and MP.8, GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.0, QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms (Bessel, Kloosterman, weight-k Laplacian, Maass–Poincaré, theta multiplier nodes; the theta multiplier is left to MP.7 there, so item 73 is not a duplicate), ClassicalArithmeticCompletion (kronecker-character).

Routes: every missing item is routed exactly once (script check: no unrouted or doubly routed item; the planned items 66 and 134 appear in source routes, which is allowed). Route stages exist. The two Part IIs (FuchsianOrbifoldsPartII, MultiquadraticPartII) have pending design jobs (queue.json), so no route goes into a finished blueprint. No cycle: GN.3 → FuchsianOrbifoldsPartII → GN.4 and GN.3 → MultiquadraticPartII → GN.4/AN.4/MP.7 are acyclic. The other FuchsianOrbifolds Part II (Bakker–Tsimerman's HyperbolicCurveVolumesAndGonality) does not overlap route 9.

Other extractions compared item by item for overlap: Bruinier–Ehlen–Yang 21 (genus character on forms, Shimura lift, harmonic Maass forms), Binyamini 22 (Duke's theorem, Siegel), Gross–Zagier 86 (E(z,s), Eisenstein at CM points = partial zeta, routed to AN.4 as here), Khayutin 19, Andreatta–Goren–Howard et al. 18, Fresán–Sabbah–Yu 22 and Xu–Zhu 22 (finite-field Kloosterman sums, which are a different object), Gan–Ichino 18 and Disegni 22 (Waldspurger, at GZ.5 as here). No Bruinier–Funke, Ghys or Li–Zhang Kudla–Rapoport extraction treats this paper's objects. Modular knots, linking numbers, Rademacher symbols, Dedekind sums, hyperbolic Fourier expansions, Kaneko's cycle integrals, traces of singular moduli and Kronecker limit formulas are not used by this paper, apart from the remark after Lemma 8 (cycle integrals give weak Maass forms, done in DIT11), so no item is owed for them.

Source issues E1–E34 each read at the locator, most on the page. Recomputed myself: E3 and E8 from the p.967 instances (with λ = 1/4 + r²); E4 and (6.3) (the product of the reduced w over the cycle equals ε_D, for D = 28, 29, 53, 173, 10205); E5's family (ℓ_A = a for D = a² + 4, a = 5, 7, 13, 101, against log ε_D ≈ 2 log a); E9 at ν = 3, β = 0; E10; E24 (7/16 = 1/4 + 3/16 and 5/12 = 1/4 + 1/6); E26 from Proposition 3 at −m; E28's part about Lemma 4 (on S_Q with a > 0, √D dz/Q(z,1) = dθ/sin θ, which is −y^{−1}|dz| in the γ_Q (clockwise) direction). The Hirzebruch–Zagier formula ℓ_J − ℓ_I = 3h(−p) was checked for every prime p ≡ 3 mod 4, 5 < p < 600, with h⁺(4p) = 2, and the D = 12 and D = 28 cycles (4), (3,2) and (3,6), (3,3,2,2,2) were recomputed. I found no further mistake in the paper; the p.967 example's (1+√−3)/2 is in the orbit of z_Q and is not one.

Errata records: research/blueprint/errata/{P}.json and .md, REV-ERRATA-{P}, research/errata/REGISTER.md and data/source-issues.json (finding 6); scripts/check_errata.py run on the errata file (finding 7).

findings.where: PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16/141 (Theorem 3, second case), statement rewritten by REV-PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16
findings.claim: The review replaced the hypothesis of item 141 with a false implication. The item now reads 'Let d', d > 0 be fundamental discriminants with D = d'd > 1; then d' and d are coprime and D is fundamental.' The product of two positive fundamental discriminants need not be coprime to them or fundamental: 5·5 = 25 (then K = Q(√25) = Q is not a real quadratic field and Cl⁺(K) is undefined), and 8·12 = 96 = 16·6 (gcd 4, not fundamental). The pre-review statement ('For coprime positive fundamental d,d′') was correct. As written, a formaliser would state Theorem 3 over pairs for which it has no meaning, or derive a false lemma.
findings.evidence: Paper, Theorem 3, published p.964: 'For the genus character χ associated to D = d′d and Re(s) = 1/2 …'; §7, p.971: 'The genus characters are in one-to-one correspondence with decompositions D = d′d, where d and d′ are fundamental discriminants' (D being the fundamental discriminant of K). Item 141 at commit 7d792492 (before the review): 'For coprime positive fundamental d,d′, Λ(s,χ_d)Λ(s,χ_{d′})=Σ_Aχ(A)∫_{C_A}E*(z,s)ds'. Item 141 now: 'Let d', d > 0 be fundamental discriminants with D = d'd > 1; then d' and d are coprime and D is fundamental.' Counterexamples: 5 and 8 and 12 are fundamental (Int.IsFundamentalDiscr, Mathlib/NumberTheory/FundamentalDiscriminant.lean:41), 25 and 96 are not. Item 139 states the hypothesis correctly ('Let D = d'd be a fundamental discriminant, with d' and d fundamental discriminants (hence coprime)').
findings.fix: Replace the first sentence of item 141 by: 'Let D > 1 be a fundamental discriminant and D = d′d a factorization into positive fundamental discriminants (equivalently, d′, d > 0 coprime fundamental discriminants; then D is fundamental).' Keep the rest.

findings.where: PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16/150 and PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16/153 (corrected (6.6) and the smooth genus equidistribution step); route 5 (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.2–AL.3); sourceIssue E6
findings.claim: The corrected form of (6.6), which is what the proof of Theorem 2 uses, rests on the Rankin–Selberg identity for the norm of the a(1) = 1 normalised Maass form, ⟨φ,φ⟩ = 2L(1,sym²φ)/cosh(πr), together with a polynomial upper bound for L(1,sym²φ). The extraction had this as item 151 (and its consequence as item 152); the review removed both as 'the extraction's own repairs'. Nothing now carries it. Item 150's note, item 153's statement ('the corrected unit-vector form of (6.6) (items 150–152)') and E6's reason ('see item 151') still point to the removed items, and route 5's reason still says it routes 'the missing Rankin–Selberg norm comparison to AL.3', but route 5's items are only 64 and 65. The corrected theorem therefore depends on an input that no item plans and no route sends anywhere.
findings.evidence: Route 5 in the result: items ['PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16/64', 'PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16/65'], reason 'The normalized standard Maass L-function belongs to AL.2, and the missing Rankin–Selberg norm comparison to AL.3.' Removed item 151 (commit 7d792492): 'Then ⟨φ,φ⟩=2L(1,sym²φ)/cosh(πr). Consequently ‖φ‖₂cosh²(πr/4)≤√2·L(1,sym²φ)^{1/2}, and L(1,sym²φ)≪_ε r^{2+ε}'. Item 150 note (current): 'The two forms agree because ‖φ‖² = 2L(1,sym²φ)/cosh(πr) (Rankin–Selberg …) and L(1,sym²φ) ≪_ε r^ε.' E6 correction: 'It follows from Theorem 4 and [12, Theorem 5] together with the Rankin–Selberg size of ‖φ‖ for the normalization a(1) = 1.' The review's route-5 verdict: 'AL.2–AL.3 plan the standard and Rankin–Selberg L-functions of Maass forms, which the corrected (6.6) needs (E6).' The input is outside the paper's text, but it is a key input of the corrected stated result (PROTOCOL §18: 'Items and nodes use the corrected statements').
findings.fix: Restore one item, status missing, routed in route 5 (AL.3): 'For an even (or odd) Hecke–Maass cusp form φ for PSL(2,Z), normalised by a(1) = 1 as in (5.7), with eigenvalue 1/4 + r² and ⟨φ,φ⟩ = ∫_F|φ|²dμ: ⟨φ,φ⟩ = 2L(1,sym²φ)/cosh(πr), and L(1,sym²φ) ≪_ε (1+r)^{A} for an absolute A (r^ε is known; any polynomial bound suffices).' Mark it as an input of the corrected (6.6), not a statement of the paper. Point items 150 and 153 and E6 at it by id.

findings.claim: The errata file (ERRATA job, reviewed by REV-ERRATA) and the extraction use the same ids for different mistakes, and give conflicting verdicts for the same mistake. Errata E12, E13, E14 are (5.1) 'φ(x)', (5.4) 'E*(s)' and the L(s;t) index; extraction E12, E13, E14 are DIT11 (2.19), Biró's Vitali step and the DIT11 U/W order, while the same three errata mistakes reappear in the extraction as E15, E16, E21. For E5, E6 and E11 the two files disagree: E5 'affects a stated result' (errata) against 'nothing'; E6 'gap/the proof' against 'error/a stated result'; E11 review verdict 'rejected' against 'confirmed'. The register therefore lists 48 entries for 34 distinct mistakes, 14 ids occur twice in data/source-issues.json, and a reader cannot tell which E12 or which E11 verdict is meant.

findings.where: PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16/63 (level-one Hecke operators on Maass forms)
findings.claim: The item says the weight-zero Hecke action must be constructed ('Use the normalized weight-zero Hecke action, T_m f(z)=m^(−1/2)Σ…'), status missing with no citation. Tau Ceti already has the double-coset slash sum on arbitrary functions ℍ → ℂ in any integer weight, including weight 0, its invariance under the second group when f is invariant under the first, and composition of such sums.
